---
title: "Uncertainty in Networks"
---

Uncertainty *is* probability.  This chapter treats inputs, parameters, and
predictions as **distributions**, not point values, and propagates that
uncertainty honestly through a model.  The engine is the same invertible map from
[Gaussianization](../gaussianization/index.qmd) — now run **backward** to
*generate* the dependence the model must carry.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## The Spine — The Same Machine, Run Backward

$$
\underbrace{z = T(x)}_{\text{forward: measure / remove}}
\qquad\qquad
\underbrace{x = T^{-1}(z)}_{\text{backward: propagate}}
$$

To carry uncertainty forward you must **sample**, and sampling *jointly* is the
whole game.  Draw an easy Gaussian sample and invert it: you recover the real,
dependent world — tails and all — which the naive "sample each variable on its
own" can never do.
:::

## Two Questions, Two Acts

Every uncertainty here is one of two questions, and the chapter is two acts:

- **Act 1 — What could the world do?**  Sample the **joint**, price the tail.
  The ladder of scenario generators, graded on one exam: *reproduce the
  co-crash, price the 1% VaR.*
- **Act 2 — How wrong is my prediction?**  A band around $\hat y = f(x)$:
  noise you must **predict** (aleatoric), ignorance you must **admit**
  (epistemic).

## The Ladder of Propagation

Act 1's rungs — each a way to *generate* the joint, mirroring the dependence
chapter's measurement ladder run in reverse:

| Rung | Method | Captures | Misses |
|------|--------|----------|--------|
| 1 | Independent resampling | marginals | all the joint structure |
| 2 | Gaussian Monte-Carlo | linear co-movement | the fat, skewed joint tail |
| 3 | Student-t Monte-Carlo | fat tails, tail dependence | the *shape* is still assumed |
| 4 | RBIG backward | the learned, real joint tail | (the hero) |
| 5 | Normalizing flows | rich learned joints | (training cost) |

Act 2's tools: predict the noise $\sigma(x)$ (in markets: **volatility**),
ensembles for model doubt, and **calibration** to check the promise was kept.

## Why It Sits Here

- **Probability under transformation** — the change-of-variables / Jacobian rule
  shared with [Gaussianization](../gaussianization/index.qmd): a distribution
  pushed through a function is reshaped by the derivative.
- **Noise propagation** — error scales with the derivative of the system; joint
  noise must keep its [dependence](../dependence/index.qmd).
- **Code:** [pyrox](https://github.com/jejjohnson/pyrox) — the Bayesian
  primitives, if you want the formal version behind the ensemble.  Figures here
  use NumPy so they render without the heavy libs.
